an1.11:1.1: “Feature of beauty” is _subhanimitta_. In early Pali, _nimitta_ is used for a feature or quality of the mind that, when focused on, promotes the growth of similar or related qualities. Thus focusing on the agreeable quality of beauty fosters the desire for that beauty. | In this chapter, the five hindrances are divided into one per Sutta to produce five Suttas, then the positive side is given, with another five Suttas. Compare [sn46.2](), [sn46.51](), and [an3.68](). | The “single thing” template, which recurs throughout this chapter, is also found occasionally in the Saṁyutta ([sn45.77:1.2](), [sn46.29:1.1]()).
an1.11:1.2: To “apply the mind irrationally” is to use the mind in a way that produces the opposite of the desired effect.
an1.16:1.1: Compare [sn46.51:13.1](). | The “feature of ugliness” is the meditation on the parts of the body or similar practices ([an6.29:6.2]()). It is one of the meditations that leads to Nibbana ([an5.61](), [an5.69](), [an5.70]()), especially through the vanquishing of sexual desire ([an7.49:2.3](), [an9.1:6.1](), [an9.3:1.1]()).
an1.16:1.2: The commentary makes six recommendations for overcoming each of the five hindrances. Some of these apply generally, namely meditation as specified in the Sutta, good friendship, and suitable conversation. I’ll mention the items peculiar to each hindrance as they come up. For sensual desire, they are sense restraint and moderation in eating.
an1.17:1.1: “Love” (_mettā_) is the unconditional wish for the happiness and welfare of all sentient beings. By overcoming ill will ([an6.13:1.1](), [an9.1:7.1](), [an9.3:7.1]()), love is the basis for the “release” of the heart in absorption ([an8.63:2.2]()), which leads to benefits numbered eight ([an8.1]()) or eleven ([an11.15]()).
an1.17:1.2: The commentary recommends reviewing the responsibility of each person for their deeds, and abundant reflection.
an1.18:1.1: The terms _ārambhadhātu nikkamadhātu parakkamadhātu_ (“initiative, persistence, and vigor”) express motion, something like “starting off, stepping out, and marching on”.
an1.18:1.2: Recommendations include moderating in eating, changing posture, perceiving light, and outdoor living.
